page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter · 2 marks

steps.label: The definition
lines: When radiation of a suitable frequency falls
on a metal surface, electrons are emitted
from the surface. This phenomenon is called
steps.margin_note: First mark. Three parts: radiation of suitable frequency, a metal surface, electrons emitted.
steps.why: Each word narrows the claim: the radiation must have a high enough frequency, the surface is a metal, and what comes out is electrons — not light and not ions.
common_mistakes: Writing radiation of any frequency. Below the threshold frequency no electrons come out at all.
Saying the metal emits light. It emits electrons.

recall.must_convey: That electrons are emitted from a metal surface when radiation of suitable frequency falls on it.
accept: electrons are emitted from the metal
light falls on a metal surface and electrons come out

steps.memory_tip: Photo then electric: light goes in, electrons come out.

steps.label: Photoelectrons and threshold frequency
steps.mark_note: Emission only at or above ν₀
lines: when the frequency of the radiation is at or
above a minimum value called the threshold
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Name the photoelectrons and the threshold frequency ν₀.
steps.why: The words suitable frequency in the definition stand for a real condition: each metal has a threshold frequency ν₀, and radiation below ν₀ emits no electrons at any intensity.
common_mistakes: Saying stronger light always causes emission. Below ν₀ no intensity produces photoelectrons.
Calling ν₀ the threshold wavelength. ν₀ is a frequency; the threshold wavelength is c/ν₀.

recall.must_convey: That the emitted electrons are photoelectrons and emission needs the frequency to be at or above the threshold frequency ν₀.
reject: electrons are emitted from the metal

steps.memory_tip: Name both: photoelectrons for the particles, ν₀ for the frequency floor.

insider_note: The definition alone reads as one mark; the second comes from naming the photoelectrons and the threshold frequency ν₀.
